purpose: Execute the cheapest exact-source no-real-external-effect discriminator for the current EffectGate topology before the active WP105 lane chooses a production adapter shape.
hypothesis: The admitted canonical EffectGate is a single authority-owned transaction: journal PENDING and lease are established before EntityOSBridge.run, EffectGate itself invokes at most one bridge action, then finalizes the journal and releases the lease. Therefore treating EffectGate.execute as an authorization-only callback followed by a separate Frankenstein executor is structurally unsafe.
counterhypothesis: The bound implementation can be safely split into authorization and later Frankenstein dispatch without changing canonical authority semantics.

run the real bound EffectGate against a temporary UnifiedDB and an in-process fake EntityOS bridge
observe a PENDING journal row and live canonical lease inside bridge.run
require exactly one bridge.run call and VERIFIED journal state after return
retry the same canonical episode and require zero second dispatch

decision_rule: If the exact-source falsifier passes, prefer a single canonical EffectGate-owned execution port with F2 pre/post correlation and separate completion verification. Do not use the current two-stage authorize-then-F2-executor shape against EffectGate.execute.
